### When the issue title changes

`updateIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` checks the actor’s organization scope, permission, and that the issue is not archived. It calls `updateIssue` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`, which writes the new title and returns the updated row. The service then emits `issue.updated`.

At server startup, `src/instrumentation.ts` calls `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`. That registers `registerSearchListeners` from `src/server/services/search-service.ts`. Its `issue.updated` handler re-reads the issue from the repository and calls `indexIssue`; re-reading means it indexes the stored row rather than relying on event data. `indexIssue` passes the title and description, joined with a newline, to `upsertSearchDocument` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`. That upsert updates the existing document for the same organization, kind, and issue ID, or inserts one if needed.

The event bus’s `emit` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` waits for its handlers to settle before returning, so the usual update path finishes indexing before `updateIssue` returns. A handler failure is captured rather than rethrown, so it does not fail the issue write. `runSearchReindexJob` in `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts` can rebuild documents for an organization; it reuses the same indexing functions.

The `search_index` table is defined in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`. Each document stores the organization ID, subject kind and ID, optional project ID, searchable content, and indexing timestamp. Issue content is title plus description; comment content is its body; project content is name plus description. Status is not part of the stored search content.

### When someone searches

The command palette debounces input in `src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx`. When advanced search is enabled, `parseSearchQuery` in `src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts` recognizes `kind:`/`in:` and `project:` tokens and sends the remaining text with the resulting filters. The palette calls `GET` in `src/app/api/search/route.ts`, which checks organization access, the command-palette flag, and the `searchQuerySchema` in `src/schemas/search.ts` before calling `search`. The Server Action route, `searchAction` in `src/actions/search/search.ts`, applies similar checks; the full-page route in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx` validates the query and calls the same service.

In `search` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`, the service checks organization scope and `issue:read` permission, consumes the organization’s search rate limit, and evaluates the `advanced_search` flag for the organization and actor. **A query containing a colon is refused with “Field-scoped search is not included in this plan” when that flag is off**—even if the colon is literal text in an issue title. The flag is plan-gated in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` (enterprise by default, with applicable overrides). Other entry checks can also refuse a request, such as invalid query length, lack of access, or a depleted rate limit.

If those checks pass, `search` calls `searchDocuments` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`. It matches the content with a substring `LIKE` query and filters by organization, requested kinds, and optional project ID. It counts matches and returns a page ordered by indexing time and ID. The service maps rows to hits: the first content line becomes the title, `snippetAround` builds context around the query, and `hrefFor` supplies the link.
